sections.title: Quick answer

body: **The four preferences: what is shared**

Introversion describes a tendency to direct attention and energy inward. Sensing gives weight to concrete details and experience. Feeling considers people and values in decisions. Perceiving leaves room for new information or options when dealing with the outside world. None of these preferences sets a person's abilities or fixes what they will do in a given situation.

The common ISFP writing says only that these four tendencies are shared. F in particular sits at "on what basis is a judgement made"; it is neither a synonym for being emotional nor a measure of empathy. Common ISFP narratives put personal value, first-hand experience and keeping options together, and that part is a habit of description; shared letters do not bring shared experience, resources, wishes or abilities. Adventurer and Artist are nicknames and guarantee no artistic talent, no particular occupation and no preference for a risky life.
**A/T: two ends of one line, not a new dimension**

The [NERIS theory](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) introduces the Identity line: A for Assertive, T for Turbulent; in the same model S and P are called Observant and Prospecting. It covers self-assessment, self-assurance and the response to pressure, and it is **not a fifth official MBTI dimension**, nor does it judge whose cognition is more accurate. Similar four letters do not prove that the items, scoring and validity of NERIS, official MBTI and the FermatMind assessment are equivalent to each other.

The [Identity definition](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) covers confidence in your decisions and how you feel under pressure, including during setbacks or evaluation. In the same situation, two people could check the same evidence and reach the same conclusion while feeling differently about their work. The definition alone cannot tell you who will notice an issue, review it or recover from criticism faster.

The same person can be very certain about familiar work and check repeatedly under unfamiliar requirements. The following four questions have to be answered separately and cannot be merged into one impression:

- Do I approve of my own expression?
- Can a reader use it to complete the task?
- Has the other person genuinely agreed to take part?
- Has the promised responsibility been completed?
The comparison and the scenes below set out the same event side by side, without deciding by suffix who should hold and who should give way, and without assigning one approach to a fixed end.
sections.title: What the two share and where they differ

Every row belongs to the Identity line and does not involve I/E, S/N, T/F or J/P; speaking up, revising, continuing or pausing can all be adopted at either end.

| The scene observed | Which axis | What ISFP-A may attend to more | What ISFP-T may attend to more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| The work is not selected | Identity: whether the result is read as an assessment of the self | May read the rejection as this one result and keep some assurance in the original judgement | May feel less confident about their judgment after the same rejection |

Look at the exact words, the use, the resources, the consent and the actual result, which carry more information than the assurance or the worry at the time. Neither end can skip necessary facts, delivery or the other person's choice, and both can learn, revise or stop.
sections.title: Row by row comparison

body: **The poster date is hard to find: explaining and revising belong to neither end**

In this fictional example, an organiser tells two designers that the date is hard to find on their poster. Both can check the same layout and agree the date needs to be easier to find. One may still feel confident about the overall design and another may question their wider judgement. The way either person edits the poster cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Whichever reaction occurs, it is still unconfirmed whether the date is right, where readers look and what this poster has to accomplish. Have the person responsible for the event check the current facts first, then ask a few willing readers to find the date and the sign-up entry at the actual size:

- **The fact is wrong**: correct it and check again.
- **The fact is right but hard to find**: adjust one position, font size or level, then try again.

Keep the elements that still work. A limited number of trial readings supports only this version, does not prove that everyone can understand it, and cannot replace other necessary conditions. When the agreed requirement is met, the use is confirmed and no new problem appears, this round can end, and the final file can be confirmed as actually received. A new audience, a new format or a new use needs its resources and scope discussed separately; this round of feedback is not aimed at judging who has more talent.
**Exhibition tickets are booked: a change can be proposed, but the real answer has to be heard**

In this fictional example, two people have already agreed to attend an exhibition, bought tickets and learned about a new event. Either person can suggest a change. After the same objection, one might still feel comfortable with how they raised the idea and another might second-guess whether they had been considerate. The wording and the eventual decision cannot identify an A/T suffix.
Ask which part of the arrangement the other person is most looking forward to, check the booking, the transport, the preparation and the cancellation conditions, then compare:

The other person may disagree, and you may state your own needs. A new invitation that is not accepted does not automatically become an obligation, and a unilateral expense made without consent does not automatically fall to the other person. If the change causes real inconvenience, agree a workable repair and complete it, but do not trade the repair for immediate forgiveness. When time is needed to think, state a realistic time for a reply; both sides may keep what they do not wish to disclose. Real pressure or a safety problem is handled separately and not at this layer.
**The work is not selected: with the reason unknown, the follow-up and the commitments stay as they were**

In this fictional selection, two people get the same rejection with no explanation. One might see it as a single result and remain confident in the work overall. Another might feel less sure about their ability. Either could revise the same draft or start a new piece. The action and the rejection cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Not being selected says only this one thing; it does not prove overall ability, nor that the selectors were biased. If there is a specific evaluation, revise according to it; if there is none, keep "the reason is unknown".

At the same time, check the state and return date of any borrowed material, the other deliverables and the deliveries already promised. A handover has to be explicitly accepted by someone qualified, authorised and with capacity; saying it out loud does not mean it is complete, and if it genuinely cannot be met, negotiate promptly. Afterwards, with the real time, budget and support in view, choose between revising for the specific feedback, doing another exercise or resting first. Producing a new piece immediately does not prove recovery, and revising the old draft repeatedly does not prove greater care. To use an experience like this to explore a career, the training, the qualifications, the daily tasks of the whole post and the hours and pay still have to be looked at separately; the example here is not enough to choose a direction.
sections.title: Work and relationship scenes

body: **These differences cannot be used to draw conclusions about anyone else**

- **A does not mean more authentic, and T does not mean more artistic sensibility or better understanding of people.** Neither self-assurance nor worry is evidence of a result, nor evidence of understanding others; that needs training, real tasks and the other person's response.
- **A need not be more willing to take risks, and T need not be more yielding.** I/E, A/T, familiarity and real risk are different questions; a single reaction, a choice on the spot or the number of matches in a table cannot determine a type.
- **S does not exclude imagination, P does not exclude planning, F does not exclude logic.** A preference word is not a ban on an ability and guarantees no fixed behaviour; a suffix certainly does not create a new layer of function.
- **Changing more does not mean doing it right, and satisfaction does not mean completion.** Check the facts, the use and the necessary requirements first, and do not replace accuracy with more praise or a self-defined sense of completion; a real gap is handled, and an added scope needs consent.
- **Pressure is not a diagnosis of a suffix.** A shortage of resources, persistent conflict and long-running distress have to be understood from the actual situation; a label cannot decide whether to seek help, nor require anyone to carry more.

A change of result cannot on its own prove growth, regression or a change of personality; the instrument, the timing, the method of measurement and the situation all have to be looked at separately. This page offers no threshold, no prevalence figures and no prediction of an ideal partner.
sections.title: Avoiding misreadings

body: **Choose by situation, not by person**

This section is not about picking a side but about describing a fit: in some situations, one end's account may be closer to your experience. In another situation, the other end may be closer, and that is normal.

- **Familiar tasks, clear standards, reversible consequences**: note how much assurance in the original judgement remains after checking. Either end may check against the same standard, and the number of checks cannot assign an end.
- **Unfamiliar requirements and vague feedback**: after the same rejection, you might still trust your broader judgement or find yourself doubting it. The reaction cannot explain why the work was rejected. Be clear about what feedback you actually received.
- **A decision that affects someone else**: you could feel confident or less certain about your judgement after hearing the same objection. Either reaction still leaves the question of what the other person wants and what you are both willing to agree to.
- **Long periods of high load, too little sleep, repeated evaluation**: sensitivity to pressure shows more easily, and being closer to the T-end description then does not mean that is how you always are, nor that you have regressed.

For each event, record what you knew at the time, how the event affected your confidence and what happened after you checked the facts. Record examples that do not fit the pattern you expected. The exercise can help you notice changes in self-assessment, and it has no cutoff for identifying a suffix or validating a test.

body: **Framework sources**

Official MBTI describes the four preferences, and separate material describes the processes in type dynamics; A/T belongs to the NERIS Identity extension of 16Personalities, and its definition and the two ends' self-descriptions come from that site's articles. Using similar letters does not mean different tools are fully equivalent. Type descriptions and cognitive functions are theoretical explanations, not confirmed psychological mechanisms.

- [The four preferences and their scope of use](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [The source and framework of A/T](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [The definition of the Identity dimension](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent)
- [The provider's Adventurer A/T comparison](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/assertive-adventurer-isfp-a-vs-turbulent-adventurer-isfp-t)
- [The official four preferences](https://www.myersbriggs.org/my-mbti-personality-type/the-mbti-preferences/)
- [Official type dynamics and the theoretical processes](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/)
- [The ethics of using type](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)
**The four-position convention used here**

Where the function stack is cited, the common four-function notation is used: ISFP as Fi–Se–Ni–Te. This page does not rewrite that arrangement according to the suffix, nor use the order of positions to infer an order of behaviour, a field of strength, a way of collaborating or who is attractive; the attitude marking of the third process is disputed and is not treated as any institution's only account. A/T sits on the line of self-assessment, a separate description from the function positions.
**Editorial fiction statement**

The three episodes on this page — the organiser saying the poster date is hard to find, the exhibition tickets booked and the wish to change to a new activity, and the work not being selected — together with the six scenes in the comparison table, are examples invented by the editors to explain the difference, and correspond to no real person, institution or selection process. The roles such as client, organiser and the other person are fictional as well.
**Scope limits**

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19 to 93, and the abstract does not state a nationally representative sample; their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types, and found overlap with some dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument versions and samples cannot be mixed.

Erford et al. (2025) reviewed 193 English-language MBTI Form M studies published from 1999 through 2024, excluding research reported in the manual. They found internal consistency estimates of 0.845–0.921 and convergent evidence with related measures. The included studies did not provide evidence on structural validity or test–retest reliability. The Form M four-letter distribution cannot estimate NERIS A/T prevalence. These findings do not establish natural types or validate NERIS A/T or the FermatMind assessment.

The scenes here are original educational examples, not clinical guidance and not a group research finding. faq.answer:
On the NERIS Identity line, the A end emphasises steadier self-assurance and less disturbance by pressure, and the T end emphasises self-doubt and sensitivity to pressure, often alongside higher standards and a wish to improve; the scope also includes how someone responds to success, setbacks, evaluation and change. It is not a conclusion about ability, artistic talent or better and worse, and not a fifth official MBTI preference.

This page sets the same poster, the same change of plan and the same rejection side by side so that self-assessment, actual action and consequence appear separately. Whether a description is close to you depends on the degree of assurance across many events and on the actual results, not on whether one sentence sounds like you.
faq.question: What is the main difference between ISFP-A and ISFP-T?

faq.answer:
No. Official MBTI describes the four preferences, and A/T belongs to the Identity extension of another framework; the two share similar letters, but the items, the scoring and the validity are not therefore equivalent.

So a FermatMind score cannot be treated as an equivalent of official MBTI or NERIS either. To understand the four preferences, read the base page first; to understand the boundary of the suffix, the two variant pages and this page are enough, and scores from different sources do not need to be converted into each other.
faq.question: Is A/T a fifth official MBTI preference?

faq.answer:
No. The T at the end is Turbulent, the third letter of the four-letter ISFP is F (Feeling), the meaning of the -T suffix is defined by NERIS, and A/T neither adds nor strengthens any cognitive function.

The function theory and the dispute over the attitude of the third process are explained on the base page; this page does not treat the suffix as a brain mechanism, nor believe that it changes the theoretical arrangement.
faq.question: Does the T in ISFP-T turn the F into Thinking?

faq.answer:
A suffix cannot rank these. Assurance does not validate that a piece of work is usable, and worry does not validate understanding others; an artistic task is judged by training, use and the finished piece, and understanding others by listening to what they say and watching the actual interaction.

A difference in taste is not a fault in itself. Neither the provider's self-report nor the scenes here prove fitness for a post, clinical health or the quality of a match.
faq.question: Who has better art, empathy or taste?

faq.answer:
Classify the criticism first, then decide what to change; none of this depends on the suffix. A factual error is corrected; if the information is right but hard to find, observe at the actual size and change the specific obstacle; if it is only a difference of taste, explain the reason; a new use needs its resources and consent discussed separately.

Keep the content that works, then check the necessary requirements and the final acceptance. There is no need to keep everything as it is because someone called you an A, nor to overturn and redo it because someone called you a T; nor does delivery have to wait until everyone approves.
faq.question: When a poster is criticised, should I hold to it or change everything?

faq.answer:
No. Familiarity, the actual requirement, the relationship, the risk and the resources at hand all affect the reaction at that moment, and a flash of assurance or worry has no decision threshold.

The two columns here are possible original scenes, not a behavioural test. Recording several events and noticing the examples that contradict your expectation carries more information than labelling from one reaction.
faq.question: Can one first reaction to criticism decide A or T?

faq.answer:
Yes. You may act directly on a familiar task and review carefully under unfamiliar requirements, and that does not require combining the two into a new test result.

Record the specific conditions, the actions, the results and the counterexamples; there is no need to type yourself by counting matches in a table, nor to require yourself to use the same approach every time.
faq.question: Can I identify with both columns?

faq.answer:
It is better not to. A change on retest cannot on its own prove growth, and A is no more mature than T; treating the suffix as a goal easily mistakes "doubting less" for "being more accurate".

What is worth practising is obtaining specific feedback, stating needs, confirming consent, completing commitments and confirming results. When the real burden is heavy or distress persists, seek professional support as needed; what is assessed is whether an action made things clearer, not whether the suffix has changed.

sections.title: Quick answer

body: **The four preferences: what is shared**

Introversion describes a tendency to direct attention and energy inward. Sensing gives weight to concrete details and experience. Feeling considers people and values in decisions. Perceiving leaves room for new information or options when dealing with the outside world. None of these preferences sets a person's abilities or fixes what they will do in a given situation.

The common ISFP writing says only that these four tendencies are shared. F in particular sits at "on what basis is a judgement made"; it is neither a synonym for being emotional nor a measure of empathy. Common ISFP narratives put personal value, first-hand experience and keeping options together, and that part is a habit of description; shared letters do not bring shared experience, resources, wishes or abilities. Adventurer and Artist are nicknames and guarantee no artistic talent, no particular occupation and no preference for a risky life.
**A/T: two ends of one line, not a new dimension**

The [NERIS theory](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) introduces the Identity line: A for Assertive, T for Turbulent; in the same model S and P are called Observant and Prospecting. It covers self-assessment, self-assurance and the response to pressure, and it is **not a fifth official MBTI dimension**, nor does it judge whose cognition is more accurate. Similar four letters do not prove that the items, scoring and validity of NERIS, official MBTI and the FermatMind assessment are equivalent to each other.

The [Identity definition](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) covers confidence in your decisions and how you feel under pressure, including during setbacks or evaluation. In the same situation, two people could check the same evidence and reach the same conclusion while feeling differently about their work. The definition alone cannot tell you who will notice an issue, review it or recover from criticism faster.

The same person can be very certain about familiar work and check repeatedly under unfamiliar requirements. The following four questions have to be answered separately and cannot be merged into one impression:

- Do I approve of my own expression?
- Can a reader use it to complete the task?
- Has the other person genuinely agreed to take part?
- Has the promised responsibility been completed?
The comparison and the scenes below set out the same event side by side, without deciding by suffix who should hold and who should give way, and without assigning one approach to a fixed end.
sections.title: What the two share and where they differ

body: The two columns describe, for the same event, the self-assessment and the experience of pressure each end may attend to more, and how it can be checked; they are not group predictions, test thresholds or a ranking of better and worse. Every row belongs to the Identity line and does not involve I/E, S/N, T/F or J/P; speaking up, revising, continuing or pausing can all be adopted at either end.

| The scene observed | Which axis | What ISFP-A may attend to more | What ISFP-T may attend to more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The organiser says the date on the poster is hard to find | Identity: self-assurance; either end can check the date and try reading at the actual size | Hearing the same date feedback, may still be confident about the overall direction of the poster | Hearing the same date feedback, may begin to doubt their overall assessment of the layout |
| Exhibition tickets are booked, and a new activity now appeals | Identity: self-assessment after a disagreement; a change needs the cost and both sides' willingness checked | Noticing the other person is also hesitating, may still feel confident about their reason for suggesting the change | Noticing the other person is also hesitating, may doubt more whether proposing the change was appropriate |
| The work is not selected | Identity: whether the result is read as an assessment of the self | May read the rejection as this one result and keep some assurance in the original judgement | May feel less confident about their judgment after the same rejection |
| The other person pauses after hearing a different preference | Identity: self-assessment when facing a pause; the reason for the pause needs confirming with them | Facing the same pause, may still feel they expressed their preference clearly | Facing the same pause, may worry that they expressed their preference poorly |
| A new use goes beyond what was agreed | Identity: confidence in their own assessment; both ends must check the scope, the authority and the capacity | Facing the same added use, may still feel confident about their estimate of the work involved | Facing the same added use, may worry they underestimated the work involved |
| Seeing more refined work of the same kind online | Identity: self-assessment after a comparison; either end can check whether the budget, the team and the authorisation are comparable | Having seen the same comparison, may still feel confident in the direction they chose | Having seen the same comparison, may feel less certain about the direction they chose |

Look at the exact words, the use, the resources, the consent and the actual result, which carry more information than the assurance or the worry at the time. Neither end can skip necessary facts, delivery or the other person's choice, and both can learn, revise or stop.
sections.title: Row by row comparison

body: **The poster date is hard to find: explaining and revising belong to neither end**

In this fictional example, an organiser tells two designers that the date is hard to find on their poster. Both can check the same layout and agree the date needs to be easier to find. One may still feel confident about the overall design and another may question their wider judgement. The way either person edits the poster cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Whichever reaction occurs, it is still unconfirmed whether the date is right, where readers look and what this poster has to accomplish. Have the person responsible for the event check the current facts first, then ask a few willing readers to find the date and the sign-up entry at the actual size:

- **The fact is wrong**: correct it and check again.
- **The fact is right but hard to find**: adjust one position, font size or level, then try again.

Keep the elements that still work. A limited number of trial readings supports only this version, does not prove that everyone can understand it, and cannot replace other necessary conditions. When the agreed requirement is met, the use is confirmed and no new problem appears, this round can end, and the final file can be confirmed as actually received. A new audience, a new format or a new use needs its resources and scope discussed separately; this round of feedback is not aimed at judging who has more talent.
**Exhibition tickets are booked: a change can be proposed, but the real answer has to be heard**

In this fictional example, two people have already agreed to attend an exhibition, bought tickets and learned about a new event. Either person can suggest a change. After the same objection, one might still feel comfortable with how they raised the idea and another might second-guess whether they had been considerate. The wording and the eventual decision cannot identify an A/T suffix.
Ask which part of the arrangement the other person is most looking forward to, check the booking, the transport, the preparation and the cancellation conditions, then compare:

The other person may disagree, and you may state your own needs. A new invitation that is not accepted does not automatically become an obligation, and a unilateral expense made without consent does not automatically fall to the other person. If the change causes real inconvenience, agree a workable repair and complete it, but do not trade the repair for immediate forgiveness. When time is needed to think, state a realistic time for a reply; both sides may keep what they do not wish to disclose. Real pressure or a safety problem is handled separately and not at this layer.
**The work is not selected: with the reason unknown, the follow-up and the commitments stay as they were**

In this fictional selection, two people get the same rejection with no explanation. One might see it as a single result and remain confident in the work overall. Another might feel less sure about their ability. Either could revise the same draft or start a new piece. The action and the rejection cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Not being selected says only this one thing; it does not prove overall ability, nor that the selectors were biased. If there is a specific evaluation, revise according to it; if there is none, keep "the reason is unknown".

At the same time, check the state and return date of any borrowed material, the other deliverables and the deliveries already promised. A handover has to be explicitly accepted by someone qualified, authorised and with capacity; saying it out loud does not mean it is complete, and if it genuinely cannot be met, negotiate promptly. Afterwards, with the real time, budget and support in view, choose between revising for the specific feedback, doing another exercise or resting first. Producing a new piece immediately does not prove recovery, and revising the old draft repeatedly does not prove greater care. To use an experience like this to explore a career, the training, the qualifications, the daily tasks of the whole post and the hours and pay still have to be looked at separately; the example here is not enough to choose a direction.
sections.title: Work and relationship scenes

body: **These differences cannot be used to draw conclusions about anyone else**

- **A does not mean more authentic, and T does not mean more artistic sensibility or better understanding of people.** Neither self-assurance nor worry is evidence of a result, nor evidence of understanding others; that needs training, real tasks and the other person's response.
- **A need not be more willing to take risks, and T need not be more yielding.** I/E, A/T, familiarity and real risk are different questions; a single reaction, a choice on the spot or the number of matches in a table cannot determine a type.
- **S does not exclude imagination, P does not exclude planning, F does not exclude logic.** A preference word is not a ban on an ability and guarantees no fixed behaviour; a suffix certainly does not create a new layer of function.
- **Changing more does not mean doing it right, and satisfaction does not mean completion.** Check the facts, the use and the necessary requirements first, and do not replace accuracy with more praise or a self-defined sense of completion; a real gap is handled, and an added scope needs consent.
- **Pressure is not a diagnosis of a suffix.** A shortage of resources, persistent conflict and long-running distress have to be understood from the actual situation; a label cannot decide whether to seek help, nor require anyone to carry more.

A change of result cannot on its own prove growth, regression or a change of personality; the instrument, the timing, the method of measurement and the situation all have to be looked at separately. This page offers no threshold, no prevalence figures and no prediction of an ideal partner.
sections.title: Avoiding misreadings

body: **Choose by situation, not by person**

This section is not about picking a side but about describing a fit: in some situations, one end's account may be closer to your experience. In another situation, the other end may be closer, and that is normal.

- **Familiar tasks, clear standards, reversible consequences**: note how much assurance in the original judgement remains after checking. Either end may check against the same standard, and the number of checks cannot assign an end.
- **Unfamiliar requirements and vague feedback**: after the same rejection, you might still trust your broader judgement or find yourself doubting it. The reaction cannot explain why the work was rejected. Be clear about what feedback you actually received.
- **A decision that affects someone else**: you could feel confident or less certain about your judgement after hearing the same objection. Either reaction still leaves the question of what the other person wants and what you are both willing to agree to.
- **Long periods of high load, too little sleep, repeated evaluation**: sensitivity to pressure shows more easily, and being closer to the T-end description then does not mean that is how you always are, nor that you have regressed.

For each event, record what you knew at the time, how the event affected your confidence and what happened after you checked the facts. Record examples that do not fit the pattern you expected. The exercise can help you notice changes in self-assessment, and it has no cutoff for identifying a suffix or validating a test.

body: **Framework sources**

Official MBTI describes the four preferences, and separate material describes the processes in type dynamics; A/T belongs to the NERIS Identity extension of 16Personalities, and its definition and the two ends' self-descriptions come from that site's articles. Using similar letters does not mean different tools are fully equivalent. Type descriptions and cognitive functions are theoretical explanations, not confirmed psychological mechanisms.

- [The four preferences and their scope of use](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [The source and framework of A/T](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [The definition of the Identity dimension](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent)
- [The provider's Adventurer A/T comparison](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/assertive-adventurer-isfp-a-vs-turbulent-adventurer-isfp-t)
- [The official four preferences](https://www.myersbriggs.org/my-mbti-personality-type/the-mbti-preferences/)
- [Official type dynamics and the theoretical processes](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/)
- [The ethics of using type](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)
**The four-position convention used here**

Where the function stack is cited, the common four-function notation is used: ISFP as Fi–Se–Ni–Te. This page does not rewrite that arrangement according to the suffix, nor use the order of positions to infer an order of behaviour, a field of strength, a way of collaborating or who is attractive; the attitude marking of the third process is disputed and is not treated as any institution's only account. A/T sits on the line of self-assessment, a separate description from the function positions.
**Editorial fiction statement**

The three episodes on this page — the organiser saying the poster date is hard to find, the exhibition tickets booked and the wish to change to a new activity, and the work not being selected — together with the six scenes in the comparison table, are examples invented by the editors to explain the difference, and correspond to no real person, institution or selection process. The roles such as client, organiser and the other person are fictional as well.
**Scope limits**

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19 to 93, and the abstract does not state a nationally representative sample; their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types, and found overlap with some dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument versions and samples cannot be mixed.

Erford et al. (2025) reviewed 193 English-language MBTI Form M studies published from 1999 through 2024, excluding research reported in the manual. They found internal consistency estimates of 0.845–0.921 and convergent evidence with related measures. The included studies did not provide evidence on structural validity or test–retest reliability. The Form M four-letter distribution cannot estimate NERIS A/T prevalence. These findings do not establish natural types or validate NERIS A/T or the FermatMind assessment.

The scenes here are original educational examples, not clinical guidance and not a group research finding. These materials are not for hiring screening, relationship prediction or ranking ability; matters involving health and safety follow professional guidance, and help should be sought first, with no type used in place of a judgement.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
**The four preferences: what is shared**

Introversion describes a tendency to direct attention and energy inward. Sensing gives weight to concrete details and experience. Feeling considers people and values in decisions. Perceiving leaves room for new information or options when dealing with the outside world. None of these preferences sets a person's abilities or fixes what they will do in a given situation.

The common ISFP writing says only that these four tendencies are shared. F in particular sits at "on what basis is a judgement made"; it is neither a synonym for being emotional nor a measure of empathy. Common ISFP narratives put personal value, first-hand experience and keeping options together, and that part is a habit of description; shared letters do not bring shared experience, resources, wishes or abilities. Adventurer and Artist are nicknames and guarantee no artistic talent, no particular occupation and no preference for a risky life.

**A/T: two ends of one line, not a new dimension**

The [NERIS theory](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory) introduces the Identity line: A for Assertive, T for Turbulent; in the same model S and P are called Observant and Prospecting. It covers self-assessment, self-assurance and the response to pressure, and it is **not a fifth official MBTI dimension**, nor does it judge whose cognition is more accurate. Similar four letters do not prove that the items, scoring and validity of NERIS, official MBTI and the FermatMind assessment are equivalent to each other.

The [Identity definition](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent) covers confidence in your decisions and how you feel under pressure, including during setbacks or evaluation. In the same situation, two people could check the same evidence and reach the same conclusion while feeling differently about their work. The definition alone cannot tell you who will notice an issue, review it or recover from criticism faster.

The same person can be very certain about familiar work and check repeatedly under unfamiliar requirements. The following four questions have to be answered separately and cannot be merged into one impression:

- Do I approve of my own expression?
- Can a reader use it to complete the task?
- Has the other person genuinely agreed to take part?
- Has the promised responsibility been completed?

The comparison and the scenes below set out the same event side by side, without deciding by suffix who should hold and who should give way, and without assigning one approach to a fixed end.
sections.title: What the two share and where they differ

sections.body_md:
The two columns describe, for the same event, the self-assessment and the experience of pressure each end may attend to more, and how it can be checked; they are not group predictions, test thresholds or a ranking of better and worse. Every row belongs to the Identity line and does not involve I/E, S/N, T/F or J/P; speaking up, revising, continuing or pausing can all be adopted at either end.

| The scene observed | Which axis | What ISFP-A may attend to more | What ISFP-T may attend to more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The organiser says the date on the poster is hard to find | Identity: self-assurance; either end can check the date and try reading at the actual size | Hearing the same date feedback, may still be confident about the overall direction of the poster | Hearing the same date feedback, may begin to doubt their overall assessment of the layout |
| Exhibition tickets are booked, and a new activity now appeals | Identity: self-assessment after a disagreement; a change needs the cost and both sides' willingness checked | Noticing the other person is also hesitating, may still feel confident about their reason for suggesting the change | Noticing the other person is also hesitating, may doubt more whether proposing the change was appropriate |
| The work is not selected | Identity: whether the result is read as an assessment of the self | May read the rejection as this one result and keep some assurance in the original judgement | May feel less confident about their judgment after the same rejection |
| The other person pauses after hearing a different preference | Identity: self-assessment when facing a pause; the reason for the pause needs confirming with them | Facing the same pause, may still feel they expressed their preference clearly | Facing the same pause, may worry that they expressed their preference poorly |
| A new use goes beyond what was agreed | Identity: confidence in their own assessment; both ends must check the scope, the authority and the capacity | Facing the same added use, may still feel confident about their estimate of the work involved | Facing the same added use, may worry they underestimated the work involved |
| Seeing more refined work of the same kind online | Identity: self-assessment after a comparison; either end can check whether the budget, the team and the authorisation are comparable | Having seen the same comparison, may still feel confident in the direction they chose | Having seen the same comparison, may feel less certain about the direction they chose |

Look at the exact words, the use, the resources, the consent and the actual result, which carry more information than the assurance or the worry at the time. Neither end can skip necessary facts, delivery or the other person's choice, and both can learn, revise or stop.
sections.title: Row by row comparison

sections.body_md:
**The poster date is hard to find: explaining and revising belong to neither end**

In this fictional example, an organiser tells two designers that the date is hard to find on their poster. Both can check the same layout and agree the date needs to be easier to find. One may still feel confident about the overall design and another may question their wider judgement. The way either person edits the poster cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Whichever reaction occurs, it is still unconfirmed whether the date is right, where readers look and what this poster has to accomplish. Have the person responsible for the event check the current facts first, then ask a few willing readers to find the date and the sign-up entry at the actual size:

- **The fact is wrong**: correct it and check again.
- **The fact is right but hard to find**: adjust one position, font size or level, then try again.

Keep the elements that still work. A limited number of trial readings supports only this version, does not prove that everyone can understand it, and cannot replace other necessary conditions. When the agreed requirement is met, the use is confirmed and no new problem appears, this round can end, and the final file can be confirmed as actually received. A new audience, a new format or a new use needs its resources and scope discussed separately; this round of feedback is not aimed at judging who has more talent.

**Exhibition tickets are booked: a change can be proposed, but the real answer has to be heard**

In this fictional example, two people have already agreed to attend an exhibition, bought tickets and learned about a new event. Either person can suggest a change. After the same objection, one might still feel comfortable with how they raised the idea and another might second-guess whether they had been considerate. The wording and the eventual decision cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Ask which part of the arrangement the other person is most looking forward to, check the booking, the transport, the preparation and the cancellation conditions, then compare:

- keeping the original arrangement and going to the exhibition;
- making an adjustment both agree to;
- going to the new activity on another day.

The other person may disagree, and you may state your own needs. A new invitation that is not accepted does not automatically become an obligation, and a unilateral expense made without consent does not automatically fall to the other person. If the change causes real inconvenience, agree a workable repair and complete it, but do not trade the repair for immediate forgiveness. When time is needed to think, state a realistic time for a reply; both sides may keep what they do not wish to disclose. Real pressure or a safety problem is handled separately and not at this layer.

**The work is not selected: with the reason unknown, the follow-up and the commitments stay as they were**

In this fictional selection, two people get the same rejection with no explanation. One might see it as a single result and remain confident in the work overall. Another might feel less sure about their ability. Either could revise the same draft or start a new piece. The action and the rejection cannot identify an A/T suffix.

Not being selected says only this one thing; it does not prove overall ability, nor that the selectors were biased. If there is a specific evaluation, revise according to it; if there is none, keep "the reason is unknown".

At the same time, check the state and return date of any borrowed material, the other deliverables and the deliveries already promised. A handover has to be explicitly accepted by someone qualified, authorised and with capacity; saying it out loud does not mean it is complete, and if it genuinely cannot be met, negotiate promptly. Afterwards, with the real time, budget and support in view, choose between revising for the specific feedback, doing another exercise or resting first. Producing a new piece immediately does not prove recovery, and revising the old draft repeatedly does not prove greater care. To use an experience like this to explore a career, the training, the qualifications, the daily tasks of the whole post and the hours and pay still have to be looked at separately; the example here is not enough to choose a direction.
sections.title: Work and relationship scenes

sections.body_md:
**These differences cannot be used to draw conclusions about anyone else**

- **A does not mean more authentic, and T does not mean more artistic sensibility or better understanding of people.** Neither self-assurance nor worry is evidence of a result, nor evidence of understanding others; that needs training, real tasks and the other person's response.
- **A need not be more willing to take risks, and T need not be more yielding.** I/E, A/T, familiarity and real risk are different questions; a single reaction, a choice on the spot or the number of matches in a table cannot determine a type.
- **S does not exclude imagination, P does not exclude planning, F does not exclude logic.** A preference word is not a ban on an ability and guarantees no fixed behaviour; a suffix certainly does not create a new layer of function.
- **Changing more does not mean doing it right, and satisfaction does not mean completion.** Check the facts, the use and the necessary requirements first, and do not replace accuracy with more praise or a self-defined sense of completion; a real gap is handled, and an added scope needs consent.
- **Pressure is not a diagnosis of a suffix.** A shortage of resources, persistent conflict and long-running distress have to be understood from the actual situation; a label cannot decide whether to seek help, nor require anyone to carry more.

A change of result cannot on its own prove growth, regression or a change of personality; the instrument, the timing, the method of measurement and the situation all have to be looked at separately. This page offers no threshold, no prevalence figures and no prediction of an ideal partner.
sections.title: Avoiding misreadings

sections.body_md:
**Choose by situation, not by person**

This section is not about picking a side but about describing a fit: in some situations, one end's account may be closer to your experience. In another situation, the other end may be closer, and that is normal.

- **Familiar tasks, clear standards, reversible consequences**: note how much assurance in the original judgement remains after checking. Either end may check against the same standard, and the number of checks cannot assign an end.
- **Unfamiliar requirements and vague feedback**: after the same rejection, you might still trust your broader judgement or find yourself doubting it. The reaction cannot explain why the work was rejected. Be clear about what feedback you actually received.
- **A decision that affects someone else**: you could feel confident or less certain about your judgement after hearing the same objection. Either reaction still leaves the question of what the other person wants and what you are both willing to agree to.
- **Long periods of high load, too little sleep, repeated evaluation**: sensitivity to pressure shows more easily, and being closer to the T-end description then does not mean that is how you always are, nor that you have regressed.

For each event, record what you knew at the time, how the event affected your confidence and what happened after you checked the facts. Record examples that do not fit the pattern you expected. The exercise can help you notice changes in self-assessment, and it has no cutoff for identifying a suffix or validating a test.
sections.title: Which end is closer in which situation

items.answer:
On the NERIS Identity line, the A end emphasises steadier self-assurance and less disturbance by pressure, and the T end emphasises self-doubt and sensitivity to pressure, often alongside higher standards and a wish to improve; the scope also includes how someone responds to success, setbacks, evaluation and change. It is not a conclusion about ability, artistic talent or better and worse, and not a fifth official MBTI preference.

This page sets the same poster, the same change of plan and the same rejection side by side so that self-assessment, actual action and consequence appear separately. Whether a description is close to you depends on the degree of assurance across many events and on the actual results, not on whether one sentence sounds like you.
items.question: What is the main difference between ISFP-A and ISFP-T?

items.answer:
No. Official MBTI describes the four preferences, and A/T belongs to the Identity extension of another framework; the two share similar letters, but the items, the scoring and the validity are not therefore equivalent.

So a FermatMind score cannot be treated as an equivalent of official MBTI or NERIS either. To understand the four preferences, read the base page first; to understand the boundary of the suffix, the two variant pages and this page are enough, and scores from different sources do not need to be converted into each other.
items.question: Is A/T a fifth official MBTI preference?

items.answer:
No. The T at the end is Turbulent, the third letter of the four-letter ISFP is F (Feeling), the meaning of the -T suffix is defined by NERIS, and A/T neither adds nor strengthens any cognitive function.

The function theory and the dispute over the attitude of the third process are explained on the base page; this page does not treat the suffix as a brain mechanism, nor believe that it changes the theoretical arrangement.
items.question: Does the T in ISFP-T turn the F into Thinking?

items.answer:
A suffix cannot rank these. Assurance does not validate that a piece of work is usable, and worry does not validate understanding others; an artistic task is judged by training, use and the finished piece, and understanding others by listening to what they say and watching the actual interaction.

A difference in taste is not a fault in itself. Neither the provider's self-report nor the scenes here prove fitness for a post, clinical health or the quality of a match.
items.question: Who has better art, empathy or taste?

items.answer:
Classify the criticism first, then decide what to change; none of this depends on the suffix. A factual error is corrected; if the information is right but hard to find, observe at the actual size and change the specific obstacle; if it is only a difference of taste, explain the reason; a new use needs its resources and consent discussed separately.

Keep the content that works, then check the necessary requirements and the final acceptance. There is no need to keep everything as it is because someone called you an A, nor to overturn and redo it because someone called you a T; nor does delivery have to wait until everyone approves.
items.question: When a poster is criticised, should I hold to it or change everything?

items.answer:
No. Familiarity, the actual requirement, the relationship, the risk and the resources at hand all affect the reaction at that moment, and a flash of assurance or worry has no decision threshold.

The two columns here are possible original scenes, not a behavioural test. Recording several events and noticing the examples that contradict your expectation carries more information than labelling from one reaction.
items.question: Can one first reaction to criticism decide A or T?

items.answer:
Yes. You may act directly on a familiar task and review carefully under unfamiliar requirements, and that does not require combining the two into a new test result.

Record the specific conditions, the actions, the results and the counterexamples; there is no need to type yourself by counting matches in a table, nor to require yourself to use the same approach every time.
items.question: Can I identify with both columns?

items.answer:
It is better not to. A change on retest cannot on its own prove growth, and A is no more mature than T; treating the suffix as a goal easily mistakes "doubting less" for "being more accurate".

What is worth practising is obtaining specific feedback, stating needs, confirming consent, completing commitments and confirming results. When the real burden is heavy or distress persists, seek professional support as needed; what is assessed is whether an action made things clearer, not whether the suffix has changed.
items.question: Should moving from T to A be a goal of practice?

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources**

Official MBTI describes the four preferences, and separate material describes the processes in type dynamics; A/T belongs to the NERIS Identity extension of 16Personalities, and its definition and the two ends' self-descriptions come from that site's articles. Using similar letters does not mean different tools are fully equivalent. Type descriptions and cognitive functions are theoretical explanations, not confirmed psychological mechanisms.

- [The four preferences and their scope of use](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts)
- [The source and framework of A/T](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/our-theory)
- [The definition of the Identity dimension](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/identity-assertive-vs-turbulent)
- [The provider's Adventurer A/T comparison](https://www.16personalities.com/articles/assertive-adventurer-isfp-a-vs-turbulent-adventurer-isfp-t)
- [The official four preferences](https://www.myersbriggs.org/my-mbti-personality-type/the-mbti-preferences/)
- [Official type dynamics and the theoretical processes](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/)
- [The ethics of using type](https://www.myersbriggs.org/using-type-as-a-professional/mbti-code-of-ethics/home.htm)

**The four-position convention used here**

Where the function stack is cited, the common four-function notation is used: ISFP as Fi–Se–Ni–Te. This page does not rewrite that arrangement according to the suffix, nor use the order of positions to infer an order of behaviour, a field of strength, a way of collaborating or who is attractive; the attitude marking of the third process is disputed and is not treated as any institution's only account. A/T sits on the line of self-assessment, a separate description from the function positions.

**Editorial fiction statement**

The three episodes on this page — the organiser saying the poster date is hard to find, the exhibition tickets booked and the wish to change to a new activity, and the work not being selected — together with the six scenes in the comparison table, are examples invented by the editors to explain the difference, and correspond to no real person, institution or selection process. The roles such as client, organiser and the other person are fictional as well.

**Scope limits**

McCrae and Costa (1989) compared the 1985 MBTI with NEO-PI self and peer ratings in 267 men and 201 women aged 19 to 93, and the abstract does not state a nationally representative sample; their analysis did not support true dichotomies or qualitatively distinct types, and found overlap with some dimensions of the five-factor model. Instrument versions and samples cannot be mixed.

Erford et al. (2025) reviewed 193 English-language MBTI Form M studies published from 1999 through 2024, excluding research reported in the manual. They found internal consistency estimates of 0.845–0.921 and convergent evidence with related measures. The included studies did not provide evidence on structural validity or test–retest reliability. The Form M four-letter distribution cannot estimate NERIS A/T prevalence. These findings do not establish natural types or validate NERIS A/T or the FermatMind assessment.

The scenes here are original educational examples, not clinical guidance and not a group research finding. These materials are not for hiring screening, relationship prediction or ranking ability; matters involving health and safety follow professional guidance, and help should be sought first, with no type used in place of a judgement.

Content revised on 19 November 2026. This page is an educational summary based on public sources and makes no claim to independent clinical review.

- [A research summary](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1458465)
- [A review of Form M reliability and validity](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcad.70006)

The FermatMind assessment uses its own item bank and scoring; for its scope, see the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
